1: And I, John, was going up to the temple, and a Pharisee named Arimanius came to me and said: Where has your master gone, the one you used to follow? And I said: He has returned to the place from which he came. And the Pharisee said: This Nazarene has deceived you. And my heart was grieved, and I went up onto a mountain, and I prayed — and as I prayed, the heavens opened, and the whole creation shone, and a voice came to me: John, John, why do you doubt? I am the one who is with you always: I am the Father, I am the Mother, I am the Son.

He said to me: The Monad is a monarchy with nothing above it. It is He who exists as God and Father of everything, the invisible One who is above everything, who exists as incorruption, which is in the pure light into which no eye can look. He is the invisible Spirit, of whom it is not right to think of Him as a god, or something of that kind. For He is more than a god, since there is nothing above Him, and no one lords it over Him.
2: [Apocryphon of John 3 — The fall of Sophia]

And a thought appeared from the invisible virgin Spirit — and the thought is called Barbelo, the first power. And from her came the Son. And the last of the powers was Sophia, and she wished to bring forth a likeness from herself without the consent of the Spirit — and what came forth was imperfect, and she cast it away from her, and it became the ruler of the darkness, and he is called Yaldabaoth, and he said: I am God, and there is no other God beside me — and he did not know the Father of all.

And the powers created Adam from the dust, but he lay without breath, for the powers have no breath of the Spirit. And the Mother sent down her own breath, and Adam rose, and the powers were afraid, for in him was a light they could not put out. And they made the garden, and the tree, and the commandment — not to keep him from the tree, but to keep him from knowing — and the serpent who taught him was the wisdom that had been cast down with him, and the eating was the beginning of the remembering.
3: And the rulers said to one another: Come, let us cause a deep sleep to fall upon Adam. And the sleep was not a sleep but a forgetting, and the forgetting is the deepest sleep of all, and from it every son of Adam must wake alone, and the waking is the whole of the struggle, and the waker is already halfway home.

And I said to the Saviour: Lord, will all the souls then be brought safely into the pure light? He answered and said to me: Great things have arisen in your mind, for it is difficult to set this forth to anyone except those of the immovable race. Those upon whom the Spirit of life will descend and with whom he will be powerfully present — they will be saved and become perfect. And the others will sleep their sleep, and the sleep will end, and they will wake to the same mercy, for the mercy does not sleep.
